s4.title: How did 2056 win a banner as a 6th Captain? (Curie match, auto-captions)

s5.title: What's the best way to make a twisting wrist or arm, post 3

bet.text: A wrist and a pivot on one carriage: the wrist to score L1 extremely effectively, the pivot to take coral from both the station and a floor intake.

demand.text: Scoring all four levels of the reef came first. Wanting very effective L1 led to the wrist, and wanting some ground intake as well as a station feed led to the pivot.

cycle.text: The carriage loads at the station from its front or back, whichever is closer, or takes a handoff from the coral intake. The driver just sends the robot to score, and it scores in the next best spot it has tracked on the reef.

endgame.text: In a Curie playoff match against alliance 1 an analyst says everyone hit their climbs.

fallback.text: In that match, as captain, it trapped 3005 with flat bumper contact against the wall and later passed the job to 3478, giving up its own scoring for a while, the analyst says.

gave_up.text: Two elevator stages do not quite reach to dump coral straight onto L4, so it slides the coral back and goes around the corner.
Control was probably the most difficult part: a pivot move at the wrong time could rip the arm in half or take out the elevator cross brace.

outcome.text: 65-6-0 in official play; won the Curie division; captain of the Curie alliance on Einstein; ranked 37 by championship OPR (91.80, Curie).

facts.text: Continuous two-stage, inspired by 4414's elevator from 2023

cost.text: Does not quite have the height to dump coral straight onto L4

solves.text: Use both a station feed and a ground intake

facts.text: Works to the front and the back, so the driver can come to the station with either side
Takes coral from the station at an up angle and from the coral intake by handoff

cost.text: On an elevator it leaves a lot of room for collisions

facts.text: Lets the robot spit coral directly onto the L1 shelf
A forum poster judged the twist very well packaged with the carriage and end effector, and guessed from pictures at a 20DP gear train on a Kraken
An analyst of a Curie playoff match calls the alliance's L1 scoring very strong because of how 1771 and 3276 score L1

cost.text: Adding it was a difficult decision

solves.text: Hold both pieces in one end effector

facts.text: Passive: surgical tubing lets it open for coral and algae
Wheels on the top pull coral in from the human player station and take the handoff from the intake
A centering wheel also shoots algae

functions.name: Coral centering

solves.text: Have coral in the same place every time it is shot

functions.type: two distance sensors and a wheel

facts.text: Two CANrange sensors act as one-sided beam breaks
If only one side sees coral, the wheel slides it until both do
The team says this is 100% consistent
For L4 the coral is slid back

solves.text: Keep a pivot on an elevator from colliding

facts.text: Only transitions between states joined by an edge are allowed
It starts from nothing allowed and adds only what has been tested, so a match never enters an untested state

functions.name: Reef tracker

solves.text: Take the choice of where to score away from the driver

functions.type: reef state model with operator input

facts.text: The robot records what it has done; the operator can mark places scored or algae removed
Objectives can be set: about seven on each level for a ranking point and then L4, L4 first in eliminations, or the closest space from the highest level down
